options: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom
A substance made of two bonded elements
questions.explanation: An element is a pure substance made entirely of one kind of atom — gold is all gold atoms.
questions.misconception: A substance of two bonded elements is a compound, a mixture is not a pure substance, and molecules are built FROM elements — an element is specifically one kind of atom only.

questions.prompt: What defines which element an atom is?
questions.explanation: An atom's proton count defines its element — 6 protons is always carbon, 79 is always gold.
questions.misconception: Color, size, and discovery location have nothing to do with identity — the proton count is the element's sole definition.

questions.prompt: About how many elements occur naturally on Earth?
questions.explanation: About 90 elements occur naturally, and a few more exist only in laboratories.
questions.misconception: There are far more than a handful — about 90 natural elements combine in countless ways to make everything.

questions.prompt: What happens when elements bond together?
options: They form a compound — a new substance
questions.explanation: When different elements chemically bond, they form a compound — a new substance, like hydrogen and oxygen becoming water.
questions.misconception: Bonding creates a NEW substance (a compound), not more elements — and matter is never destroyed or made.
